drivingQuestion: What does the mishna's 'fit for sprinkling' come to exclude?
outcomeNote: Answer given; its source follows in the next unit

segments.he: רָאוּי לְהַזָּאָה – לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי? לְמַעוֹטֵי קִיבֵּל פָּחוֹת מִכְּדֵי הַזָּיָיה בִּכְלִי זֶה וּפָחוֹת מִכְּדֵי הַזָּיָיה בִּכְלִי זֶה.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: It is only with regard to blood that was received in a sacred vessel and is «fit for sprinkling» that the garment «requires laundering.» The Gemara asks: As it was already taught that when disqualified blood is sprayed on a garment, it does not require laundering, this reiteration serves «to exclude what?» The Gemara answers: It serves «to exclude» the case where a priest «received less» blood «than» is «sufficient for sprinkling in this vessel, and less than» is «sufficient for sprinkling in that vessel,» and then he mixed together the blood from the two vessels. In such a case, even though the combined amount is now enough for sprinkling, the blood did not become fit for sprinkling.
